publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vector Control and Direct Torque Control of Induction Motors
abstract: The author describes direct torque control (DTC) which is a new method of induction motor control which provides excellent performance without tachogenerator feedback. New control features are realised which include flux braking and fast starting. It is hoped that DTC drives will bring benefits to many drive applications including those previously reserved solely for DC and servomotor drives.

articleTitle: Comparison of stochastic and deterministic parameter identification algorithms for indirect vector control
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vector Control and Direct Torque Control of Induction Motors
abstract: The indirect vector control method provides accurate, rapid control of an induction machine's developed torque. To maintain the control performance, the position of the rotor flux vector has to be known accurately. In this paper, a stochastic and a deterministic state-space estimator are compared using experimental results, as regards their estimate of the rotor resistance. Simulation results are used to compare stationary and synchronous reference frame versions of the extended Kalman filter (EKF). Induction machine core losses are usually neglected due to the required increase in model complexity. However, a standard method of core loss compensation which does not require higher order estimators is shown to improve the EKF and extended Luenberger observer accuracy, while requiring only a minimal increase in computation. The experimental system used to implement vector control and online rotor resistance estimation is also described.

articleTitle: Direct torque control of induction motors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vector Control and Direct Torque Control of Induction Motors
abstract: A direct torque control system for a variable speed induction motor drive consists of two hysteresis comparators, a selection table, a flux and torque estimator, and a PID speed controller. With this control structure, the drive performance can be significantly improved when compared to field oriented control. In the paper, the principles and characteristics of a direct torque control system are considered. It is also shown that by means of a more complex selection table, the performance of the direct torque control system may be improved further.

articleTitle: Vector control: a practical approach to electric vehicles
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vector Control and Direct Torque Control of Induction Motors
abstract: The Wavedriver is a new type of vehicle power control centre which carries out all the power conversion and vehicle control functions needed for an electric vehicle (EV). The unit performs the vehicle traction drive, high rate charging, driver interface, battery management and other ancillary functions. Using the same components for multiple functions reduces cost; for example, the same power electronics are used for both motor drive and charging. Because of the integrated and highly software-based nature, adaptation to the needs of different vehicle platforms is convenient. The Wavedriver hardware platform consists of a three-phase full bridge built from liquid cooled IGBT modules. The drive is configured for induction motors. These are usually liquid cooled. A vector control scheme is used which is based on a rotor flux indirect field orientation approach. The entire control system is implemented digitally on low cost processors. To meet stringent vehicle safety standards the software is designed to UL1998 standards.

articleTitle: A simple understanding of field-orientation for AC motor control
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vector Control and Direct Torque Control of Induction Motors
abstract: In the AC motor control field, "vector" has now become a grossly abused term causing confusion e.g. as to whether it signifies an alternative to pulse-width-modulation (i.e. DC-to-AC power conversion) or a technique for AC motor torque control. To emphasise the latter meaning, the term "flux-vector control" is now widely accepted, but the confusion still continues with phrases like 'sensorless flux-vector control'. Hence, the term "field-orientation" is used here in an attempt to provide a simple understanding of field-orientation for AC motor control.

articleTitle: Detuned operation of rotor flux oriented induction machines in the field-weakening region due to iron loss
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vector Control and Direct Torque Control of Induction Motors
abstract: Iron loss, traditionally ignored in vector control schemes, inevitably causes certain detuning during operation of a rotor flux oriented induction machine. The studies that discuss detuning in the base speed region, for operation at rated speed with rated rotor flux command, are already available. However, it appears that no detuning study has been performed for the field-weakening region so far. Any such study would require identification of equivalent iron loss resistance at frequencies other than rated. The aim of this paper is twofold. Firstly, an experimental method that enables identification of equivalent iron loss resistance over the frequency range of interest is described and experimental results are presented. Then, the equivalent iron loss resistance values are utilised in evaluation of detuning in the field-weakening region, for speeds up to five times rated. Detuning in the field-weakening region is found to be significantly in excess of the one met at rated speed, if the machine operates at high speeds with relatively light loads.

articleTitle: DSP-controlled intelligent high-performance AC drives present and future
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vector Control and Direct Torque Control of Induction Motors
abstract: Two types of high performance AC motor drives are discussed. Results obtained from DSP-based implementations of a variety of AC drive configurations are presented. The advantages of the application of intelligent controllers are also discussed.
